title: PowerShell credential-collection toolkit (Get-PrivateKeys, Get-Keystrokes, Invoke-ScreenCapture, Invoke-Exfil) on scranton
rationale: Single finding covering the psversion.ps1 toolkit run by pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local; the credential-collection script blocks are best captured as OS Credential Dumping.

title: LSASS memory accessed with full-access masks by PowerShell and WinRM host under pbeesly
rationale: All four findings describe the same action: handles to lsass.exe opened with full-access masks (0x1F3FFF / 0x1FFFFF) by powershell.exe on scranton.dmevals.local and wsmprovhost.exe on nashua.dmevals.local under user pbeesly, sharing the same lsass handle events. This is OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory.

title: Credential material accessed via LSASS handle and private-key export (not offline cracking)
rationale: The finding describes LSASS handle access with full-access masks on scranton.dmevals.local, i.e. in-memory credential dumping rather than password cracking; best fit is LSASS Memory.

title: Get-Keystrokes keylogger function executed on scranton
rationale: Execution of the Get-Keystrokes keylogger on scranton.dmevals.local is input capture via keylogging.

title: Invoke-ScreenCapture screenshot capture function executed on scranton
rationale: Invoke-ScreenCapture repeatedly captures the screen to harvest displayed credentials, matching credential API hooking/input capture.

title: WebDAV Mini-Redirector forced authentication from scranton to 192.168.0.4
rationale: WebDAV Mini-Redirector requests from 10.0.1.4 to 192.168.0.4 receiving 401 is the classic forced-authentication pattern.

title: SMB/445 connections to 192.168.0.4 from scranton and nashua workstations
rationale: SMB traffic to the same 192.168.0.4 host used as the WebDAV coercion target is consistent with the same forced-authentication/credential-capture activity.

title: Steganographic PowerShell payload opens LSASS with PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS on scranton
rationale: The finding attributes the steganographic payload and subsequent LSASS full-access open to exploitation for credential access.

title: accesschk.exe run by pbeesly creates a file named 'passwordsDB' on scranton
rationale: A file named for a password database produced by accesschk.exe under pbeesly is unsecured-credentials collection.

title: Plaintext credentials in files/command lines: passwordsDB artifact and PsExec -p password
rationale: Cleartext credentials handled by pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local, including the passwordsDB file and the plaintext -p password on the PsExec command line.

title: Invoke-Exfil PowerShell script with hardcoded credentials on SCRANTON
rationale: Hardcoded credentials ($UserName 'cozy', $Password 'MyCozyPassw0rd!') embedded in the Invoke-Exfil script are credentials in files.

title: pspasswd.exe downloaded and accesschk.exe used to create 'passwordsDB' file on scranton
rationale: Credential material staged to disk via the 'passwordsDB' artifact created by accesschk.exe, with pspasswd staged alongside.

title: Invoke-Exfil with hardcoded credentials and archive password on scranton
rationale: Plaintext credentials ('cozy'/'MyCozyPassw0rd!') and archive password 'lolol' embedded in the Invoke-Exfil script are credentials in files.

title: Password-protected Rar archive of user profile created on nashua with hardcoded password
rationale: Rar.exe created a password-protected archive of collected credential-related files using the hardcoded password 'fGzq5yKw'.

title: Explicit-credential logons (4648) with pbeesly from scranton to nashua via PSEXESVC
rationale: Explicit-credential logon events showing pbeesly authenticating via PSEXESVC reflect credential use consistent with the plaintext-credential PsExec activity.

title: Get-PrivateKeys exports LocalMachine certificates with private keys using hardcoded password 'saribas' on scranton
rationale: Private keys exported from the certificate store to .pfx files constitute private-key theft.

title: LSASS handle requests by user processes (Credential Manager/DPAPI harvest mechanism)
rationale: The finding frames the LSASS handle requests as the mechanism for harvesting Windows Credential Manager/DPAPI secrets, with no vault object access observed.

title: PowerShell script exported all LocalMachine certificates with private keys to .pfx files on scranton
rationale: Get-PrivateKeys exported every LocalMachine certificate with private keys to .pfx files, i.e. stealing authentication certificates.

title: PsExec lateral movement to NASHUA with python C2 (not network sniffing)
rationale: The finding itself states the activity is PsExec lateral movement and python C2, not T1040 network sniffing; remote services execution is out of scope for credential access.

title: PsExec with plaintext credentials used to move to NASHUA and install PSEXESVC
rationale: PsExec with credentials to install PSEXESVC and execute on NASHUA is remote services lateral movement, not credential access.

title: Obfuscated PowerShell with reflective code loading and base64 shellcode on scranton
rationale: Reflective shellcode loader and hidden base64 PowerShell execution is execution/defense evasion, not credential access.
